title: Svitzer orders six more TRAnsverse 2900 tugs from Cheoy Lee, taking series to 14
summary: Svitzer placed a follow-on order with Hong Kong's Cheoy Lee Shipyards for six additional 29 m TRAnsverse tugs (80 t bollard pull, biofuel-ready, IMO Tier III, FiFi1-ready), bringing its TRA2900 order with the yard to 14 and total TRAnsverse vessels under construction worldwide to 20. Deliveries start early 2028. The order confirms the Robert Allan-designed TRAnsverse as Svitzer's standard fleet-renewal platform, with more than three-quarters of its tugs on order based on the design.

title: Svitzer contracts Swan Defence (Pipavav) to build four 32 m TRAnsverse tugs in India
summary: Svitzer awarded Swan Defence and Heavy Industries (SDHI) a contract for four 32 m Robert Allan-designed TRAnsverse harbour/escort tugs (80 t BP, biofuel/Tier III/FiFi1-ready) to be built at the Pipavav yard in Gujarat, with first deliveries from Q1 2028. It is Svitzer's second Indian newbuild programme after the Cochin Shipyard electric-tug deal, signalling a deliberate shift of fleet renewal to Indian yards and positioning for Indian port towage.

title: Svitzer orders ASD harbour tug to expand Port of Bristol operation
summary: Svitzer ordered a 23 m x 12 m ASD harbour tug (70 t BP, twin Caterpillar 3512TA) for harbour towage at the Port of Bristol, UK, with delivery scheduled for late 2026. It is the first in a planned series for Bristol, reinforcing Svitzer's UK footprint alongside its Fawley refinery and Humber operations.

title: Svitzer signs Cochin Shipyard to build four battery-electric TRAnsverse 2600e tugs; steel cut Sept 2026
summary: Following an October 2025 letter of intent signed at India Maritime Week, Svitzer contracted Cochin Shipyard Ltd for four fully electric 26 m TRAnsverse 2600e tugs (70 t BP) with options for four more; first delivery is targeted for late 2027 and steel was cut in September 2026. Initial deployment regions are Northern Europe, South America and Australia, with possible future use in Indian ports. First contracted TRAnsverse series built in India and a cornerstone of Svitzer's electrification programme.
capacity: 4 (+4 option) x 70 t BP electric tugs

title: Svitzer acquires 66.6% of Norway's Buksér og Berging, adding ~64 vessels
summary: Svitzer agreed to take a two-thirds controlling stake in Oslo-based Buksér og Berging (founded 1913), whose fleet of about 35 tugs, 25 pilot boats, ambulance and aquaculture service vessels (c.64 ships per TradeWinds) operates from Oslo, Stavanger and Fedje. CEO Vetle Sverdrup retains 33.4% and the brand and management stay separate. The deal, subject to Norwegian competition approval, is Svitzer's first major M&A since going private and strengthens its Scandinavian towage and offshore position.

title: Svitzer's Med Marine-built tugs Isla Popa and Isla Uva arrive for Panama Canal charter
summary: Two new 26 m Robert Allan TRAktor 2600-Z tractor tugs (65 t BP) built by Med Marine in Eregli, Turkey arrived in Panama to assist vessels in the locks and Culebra Cut under a charter with the Panama Canal Authority. The ACP describes the Svitzer charter as a way to expand capacity without compromising fleet-management flexibility; Svitzer's 2024 annual report cites a five-year ACP contract as a key growth win. Builds on Svitzer Americas' 100+ vessel, 13-country presence.

title: Sanmar delivers two azimuth tractor tugs to Svitzer Bahrain
summary: Svitzer took delivery of two Sanmar-built azimuth tractor tugs, renamed Svitzer Manama and Svitzer Awal, for its Bahrain operations. The delivery renews Svitzer's Gulf fleet in a market where AD Ports/Noatum (via the ASRY Marine JV) and Boluda are expanding, and is Svitzer's only reported Middle East fleet move in 2025 apart from the Oman LNG contract.

title: A.P. Moller Holding completes DKK 9bn takeover of Svitzer; shares delisted from Nasdaq Copenhagen
summary: APMH Invest's recommended all-cash offer (DKK 285/share, a 31.7% premium valuing Svitzer at c.DKK 9.0bn / USD 1.3bn, launched 2 April 2025) closed with 93.4% acceptance; the remaining shares were compulsorily acquired and Svitzer delisted by 22 May 2025, just 13 months after its April 2024 demerger from Maersk. Svitzer (c.450 vessels, 140+ ports, 40 terminals, 37 countries) is again privately held by the Maersk family holding, freeing it to pursue M&A such as Buksér og Berging.

title: Svitzer wins nine-year terminal towage contract with Oman LNG at Qalhat
summary: Svitzer signed a nine-year terminal towage contract with Oman LNG for the Qalhat LNG jetty, deploying four newbuild 65 t BP ASD tugs on time charter from early 2026 for LNG/NGL tanker towage, escort, firefighting, pilot boarding and dive support. The win adds a second Omani LNG terminal to Svitzer's AMEA portfolio and competes directly with regional towage players for Gulf energy-terminal work.

title: Svitzer FY2024: revenue DKK 6.3bn (+9%), adjusted EBITDA margin 29.9%, ~450 vessels in 37 countries
summary: Svitzer reported 2024 revenue of DKK 6,320m (DKK 5,786m in 2023), adjusted EBITDA of DKK 1,887m and gross capex of DKK 981m, with all four regions growing. Growth drivers were new contracts (incl. a five-year Panama Canal Authority deal), renewals, tariff increases and the first TRAnsverse tug in Amsterdam; the CEO flagged a slowdown in new awards. 2025 guidance: revenue +1-5%, capex DKK 1.1-1.3bn.

title: Svitzer orders four TRAnsverse 2900 tugs from Cheoy Lee with option for four more
summary: Svitzer contracted Cheoy Lee Shipyards for four 29 m, 80 t BP TRAnsverse tugs for delivery by end-2026 (plus four options), taking the number of the Robert Allan co-developed design on order to seven with one already in service. Marked the start of the series production that reached 14 units with Cheoy Lee by September 2026.

title: Svitzer orders world's first battery-methanol escort tug from Uzmar for Gothenburg; methanol gensets later swapped for diesel
summary: Svitzer ordered a battery-electric escort tug with methanol generator sets from Turkey's Uzmar (6 MWh AYK battery) for the Port of Gothenburg, expected to handle ~25% of its local work with up to 90% on battery power. In October 2026 Svitzer replaced the two methanol gensets on the delivered tug Svitzer Balder with diesel range extenders citing technical difficulties, while retaining the ~6,000 kWh battery. Illustrates both Svitzer's decarbonisation leadership and the practical limits of methanol on tugs.

title: Maersk initiates demerger and separate Nasdaq Copenhagen listing of Svitzer
summary: A.P. Moller-Maersk announced the demerger of Svitzer into a separately listed company (listed April 2024), with A.P. Moller Holding emerging as the ~47% anchor shareholder. The spin-off created the world's largest standalone listed towage operator for 13 months before APMH took it private again in May 2025.

title: Svitzer completes six-tug Rampart 2300 series from Rio Maguari for Brazilian ports
summary: Delivery of Svitzer Babitonga completed a series of six Robert Allan Rampart 2300 harbour tugs built locally by Estaleiro Rio Maguari for Svitzer's Brazilian operations, which span Salvador, Suape, Pecém, Santos, Vitória, Rio Grande, São Francisco do Sul and Paranaguá and support LNG terminals. Locally built fleet strengthens Svitzer against Wilson Sons and Boluda-backed operators in Brazil.

title: Boluda Shipping agrees to acquire Samskip, creating a 32-vessel Europe-Iberia-Canaries-West Africa shortsea network
summary: Boluda Shipping (the Boluda Lines parent) agreed to buy Rotterdam-based Samskip, with completion targeted for 1 January 2027 subject to regulatory approval. The combined business will run 32 vessels, 21 maritime and 5 rail terminals, 500+ trucks and 18 maritime routes across 28 countries linking Northern Europe with Iberia, the Canary Islands and West Africa, handling 750,000+ TEU a year. Samskip's brand and CEO stay; Rotterdam becomes the network hub. A major move into intra-European/West Africa feeder and multimodal logistics directly relevant to Unifeeder's markets.

title: Boluda Maritime Terminals wins 16-year concession for Principe d'Espanya wharf in Barcelona with EUR 40m investment
summary: Boluda Maritime Terminals secured a 16-year concession to operate the 87,425 m2 Principe d'Espanya wharf (531 m quay) in the Port of Barcelona, investing EUR 40m (EUR 28m in mobile cranes, reach stackers and electric equipment, c.EUR 10m in facility upgrades) for an expected 1.3m tonnes/yr of containers, general cargo, ro-ro, short-sea and project cargo. Extends Boluda's nine-terminal Spanish network as Marsa Maroc takes a 45% stake in the terminals arm.

title: Boluda adds Damen ASD 2811 tug VB Audace at Port Reunion (Pointe des Galets)
summary: Boluda Towage deployed the newbuild Damen ASD 2811 tug VB Audace (28.5 m, 3,800 kW, 60 t BP) at Pointe des Galets, La Reunion, from mid-September 2026 to strengthen its Indian Ocean position. Reinforces Boluda's presence on the Indian Ocean island hub that serves as a gateway to East and Southern Africa.

title: Boluda christens two new tugs in Genoa after near EUR 20m investment
summary: Boluda named VB Marte (Damen ASD 2813 built at Song Cam, Vietnam, delivered Dec 2025) and VB Insignia (Med Marine, Turkey) at Ponte Parodi, Genoa, following an investment of almost EUR 20m. Shows Boluda renewing the Italian fleet it inherited through the MedTug/Rimorchiatori Mediterranei combination with MSC.

title: VB Kudu and VB Nyala join Boluda's Cote d'Ivoire fleet, taking it to 14 tugs
summary: Boluda Towage added two tugs to its Ivorian operation run through IRES, its joint company with the Ports of Abidjan and San Pedro, bringing the fleet there to 14 tugboats. Boluda positions itself as a strategic partner in modernising Ivorian port services; Abidjan also received a Damen ASD 2312 (VB-651) in March 2026. Cote d'Ivoire is Boluda's largest West African towage base.

title: Boluda acquires Seatrium's tug fleet and shipyard towage contracts in Singapore
summary: Boluda Towage continued its acquisition push by taking over Seatrium Group's tug fleet together with its shipyard towage services and contracts, strengthening its position in Singapore and Malaysia where its Asia-Pacific fleet already exceeds 150 tugs. Value undisclosed.

title: Boluda takes delivery of five Damen tugs for Rotterdam, Tilbury and Abidjan
summary: In Q1 2026 Boluda Towage received three Damen RSD 2513 tugs (80 t BP, FiFi1: VB Foxtrot, VB Fantastic, VB Boluman) and two ASD 2312 tugs built in Vietnam and delivered by Redwise. Deployment: Rotterdam (three units), Tilbury/London (VB Boluman, first RSD on the Thames) and Abidjan, Cote d'Ivoire (VB-651). Fleet renewal across Boluda's core European hubs and West Africa.
capacity: 5 tugs (3 x 80 t BP RSD, 2 x ASD 2312)

title: Marsa Maroc to buy 45% of Boluda Maritime Terminals for EUR 80m
summary: Morocco's Marsa Maroc agreed to acquire 45% of Boluda Maritime Terminals (nine terminals in mainland Spain and the Canaries, 1m+ TEU in 2024) for EUR 80m, subject to clearance; Boluda keeps management control. For Boluda the deal brings a strategic Moroccan partner across the Strait of Gibraltar corridor and complements the Boluda-Marsa Maroc towage JV at Nador West Med.

title: Boluda completes USD 640m purchase of Boskalis/Smit Lamnalco towage business in Australia and PNG
summary: Boluda Towage acquired Royal Boskalis' towage and salvage operations in Australia and Papua New Guinea (39 tugs, c.400 staff, Sydney regional HQ) covering Sydney/Botany, Melbourne, Brisbane, Newcastle, Gladstone, Mackay, Weipa, Townsville, Launceston and Port Moresby, for about USD 600-640m. Completed 30 Sept 2025, it gives Boluda its first Australian footprint, takes its fleet past 850 vessels on five continents and settles the long-running 2023 Smit Lamnalco deal with Boskalis.

title: Boluda Towage France-Marsa Maroc JV wins 20-year towage licence at Nador West Med
summary: A 51/49 joint venture of Boluda Towage France and Marsa Maroc was awarded the 20-year licence (effective Q4 2026) for towage and assistance at Morocco's new Nador West Med transhipment port, investing EUR 45m including four newbuild 80 t harbour tugs for 2026 delivery. Locks Boluda into the Mediterranean port that will compete with Tanger Med and Algeciras, and deepens its Moroccan ties (Casablanca since 2005, Tanger Med).

title: MSC to take 49% of Boluda Towage by contributing MedTug's ~180 tugs, creating world's largest tug owner
summary: Boluda and MSC moved to close (targeted H1 2025) the combination under which MSC's MedTug (incl. Rimorchiatori Mediterranei; assets in Italy, Greece, Malta, Norway, Colombia, Malaysia, Singapore) is merged into Boluda Towage in exchange for a 49% stake, with Boluda retaining 51% and management. The combined fleet (~550+ tugs) overtakes Svitzer as the largest. MSC first bought 7% in Dec 2022 for c.EUR 87m. Pending competition approvals in several countries.

title: Boluda Lines takes delivery of 1,300 new UNIT45 dry containers for Europe-West Africa-Indian Ocean network
summary: UNIT45 delivered 1,000 x 40ft and 300 x 20ft dry containers (bamboo floors, waterborne paint) to Boluda Lines to support door-to-door services across Europe, the West African coast, Cape Verde, the Indian Ocean and Latin America. Equipment growth ahead of the Samskip acquisition signals volume expansion in Boluda's feeder/shortsea business.

title: Boluda Towage acquires Les Abeilles International emergency response fleet in France
summary: Boluda bought Les Abeilles International, the French emergency towing, salvage and anti-pollution operator with six French-flagged vessels (four tugs, one multipurpose vessel, one AHTS) serving the Atlantic and Mediterranean coasts. Adds state emergency-response contracts to Boluda Towage France, which also covers overseas territories, the African Atlantic coast and Timor-Leste.

title: Boluda Towage acquires UK's SMS Towage and its 20-tug fleet
summary: Boluda Towage agreed to acquire Hessle-based SMS Towage Ltd, including 20 tugs, its harbour and offshore towage operations, management, staff and crews, extending Boluda's UK presence beyond the Thames and Southampton. Third acquisition of 2024 after Resolve Gibraltar and the pending Smit Lamnalco deal.

title: Boluda Lines launches weekly Santander-Tilbury-Rotterdam short-sea container service
summary: Boluda Lines opened a weekly shortsea loop with an 800 TEU feeder linking Boluda Maritime Terminals' Santander container terminal with London Container Terminal (Tilbury, 3 days) and Rotterdam (+2 days). Integrates Boluda's own terminal with a north-south Atlantic feeder, foreshadowing the Samskip combination.

title: Boluda acquires Resolve Salvage & Fire's Gibraltar harbour towing operation and four tugs
summary: Boluda Towage bought the Gibraltar towing division of US-based Resolve Marine, adding four tugs (Elliot, Hercules, Rooke, Wellington) and the harbour towage franchise at the Strait of Gibraltar bunkering hub. Fills the gap between Boluda's Spanish and Moroccan operations; a further tug was added in June 2024.

title: Boluda Towage starts operations at Hutchison's Abu Qir Container Terminal, Egypt with three new 75 t tugs
summary: Boluda entered Egypt in January 2024, handling its first vessel at Abu Qir Container Terminal on 9 January with three new 75 t BP FiFi tugs (VB Amon and VB Horus from Sanmar, VB Ahmose from Med Marine) and a dedicated onshore team, with support from the Egyptian Navy and Hutchison Ports. First Boluda towage base in Egypt, competing with Svitzer (Port Said/Suez, Idku LNG) in a key Mediterranean market.

title: Boskalis H1 2026: profit down 35% to EUR 275m as Middle East disruption and Gulf closure hit dredging; Smit Lamnalco stable
summary: Boskalis reported H1 2026 revenue of EUR 1.90bn (EUR 2.35bn), EBITDA EUR 553m (748m) and net profit EUR 275m, with the order book at EUR 6.8bn. Dredging suffered from slow Asian and Middle East markets, delayed awards and very low cutter utilisation; the effective closure of the Persian Gulf hurt marine survey and fleet utilisation. Smit Lamnalco towage was stable, with a contract renewal in Gabon; the 31,000 m3 hopper Seaway and the 45,500 t Windpiper entered service. H2 EBITDA guided broadly level.

title: Boskalis-Van Oord JV wins ~EUR 500m Lulea port deepening (Malmporten), Sweden
summary: The Swedish Maritime Administration and Port of Lulea awarded a Boskalis/Van Oord 50:50 joint venture a roughly EUR 500m contract to dredge ~14m m3 of mixed material and rock to deepen the fairway and basin to take 14.7 m draught, 85,000 dwt ships (from 45,000 dwt), reusing material to reclaim a new deepwater port area. Work runs spring 2027 to mid-2030 in ice-free seasons. One of Europe's largest port dredging awards of 2026.

title: Port of Gothenburg awards Boskalis SEK 202m Skandia Gateway deepening (13.5 m to 17.5 m)
summary: Boskalis Sweden won a SEK 202m (~EUR 18m) blasting and dredging contract, selected among five bidders, to deepen the Skandia Gateway fairway at Scandinavia's largest container port from 13.5 m to 17.5 m so ULCVs can call fully laden; dredging runs October 2026 to March 2027, with the Swedish Maritime Administration deepening the outer approach from autumn 2027.

title: Smit Lamnalco renews long-term terminal towage contract in Gabon
summary: Boskalis' H1 2026 results cite the renewal of a long-term Smit Lamnalco towage contract in Gabon as one of the period's main wins, alongside UK maintenance-dredging extensions. Smit Lamnalco's remaining business after the Australian divestment is built on long-term energy-terminal contracts in the Middle East and West Africa, making Gabon a core anchor.

title: Boskalis 2025 results: record EUR 4.5bn revenue, EUR 775m net profit; Towage & Salvage doubles to EUR 0.4bn on Smit Lamnalco
summary: Boskalis reported 2025 revenue of EUR 4.5bn, EBITDA EUR 1.3bn, net profit EUR 775m and an order book of EUR 7.0bn, investing EUR 564m in the fleet (Seaway 31,000 m3 TSHD, Windpiper SRI vessel, BOKA Spearfish). Towage & Salvage revenue rose to EUR 0.4bn after full consolidation of Smit Lamnalco; key projects included Oxagon port expansion (Saudi Arabia), Pulau Tekong polder (Singapore), the ASL Bauhinia refloat towed to Jebel Ali and the Stena Immaculate salvage. EUR 237m capex committed incl. four new Smit Lamnalco vessels.

title: Boskalis completes dredging and marine works for Port of Oxagon (NEOM) expansion, Saudi Arabia
summary: Boskalis' 2025 annual results list the expansion of the Port of Oxagon at NEOM as a completed major project, following its dredging role in the BESIX-led Port of NEOM marine works. Saudi Arabia was its main Middle East dredging market in 2024-25 with cutter suction dredgers at ~51 weeks utilisation, before the regional conflict slowed Gulf awards in 2026.

title: Smit Salvage refloats burning container ship ASL Bauhinia and tows it to Jebel Ali
summary: In 2025 Smit Salvage fought a container ship fire in the Middle East, refloated the grounded ASL Bauhinia and towed it to Jebel Ali, UAE, one of two Lloyd's Open Form jobs in H1 2025 alongside the Stena Immaculate (North Sea) and Glengyle (Vietnam) cases. Demonstrates Boskalis' emergency-response capability in the Gulf, a service line DP World's own marine arm does not offer.

title: Boskalis completes sale of Smit Lamnalco Australia and PNG towage to Boluda for ~USD 640m
summary: Boskalis signed in June 2025 and completed on 30 September 2025 the sale of Smit Lamnalco's Australian and Papua New Guinean harbour towage and salvage business (39 tugs, 11 ports) to Boluda Towage, reported at USD 600-640m. Boskalis has sought to exit global harbour towage since 2019; it retains Smit Lamnalco's long-term terminal contracts in the Middle East and West Africa.

title: Smit Lamnalco wins 10-year ExxonMobil Guyana contract, orders four 130 t DP2 terminal support vessels in Turkey
summary: Smit Lamnalco secured a ten-year contract with ExxonMobil Guyana for offshore FPSO terminal support and signed shipbuilding contracts with a Turkish yard for four Robert Allan-designed 60 m terminal support vessels (130+ t BP, DP2, FiFi1). Boskalis cites the award, part of ~EUR 0.9bn of new orders in July 2025, as a flagship for Smit Lamnalco's refocused offshore-terminal strategy in a growing oil province.

title: Boskalis-Allseas consortium wins ~EUR 1.2bn CPC YT2 offshore gas pipeline in Taiwan
summary: CPC Corporation awarded a 50/50 Boskalis-Allseas consortium the design, construction and installation of the 232 km, 36-inch YT2 gas pipeline from Yongan LNG terminal to Tongxiao. Boskalis handles landfalls, microtunnelling, trenching, backfill and rock installation for 34 crossings, deploying two large hoppers, a backhoe dredger and an SRI vessel; execution 2026-2028. Reinforces Boskalis' pivot to energy-transition seabed work in Asia.

title: Boskalis returns to Benin for 3.5m m3 sand nourishment coastal protection at Avlekete
summary: Boskalis began a new coastal protection project in Benin using a trailing suction hopper dredger to place more than 3.5m m3 of sand around an existing 5 km underwater breakwater to protect Avlekete beach, about two years after completing a 6.4m m3 sand motor there in 2022. Keeps Boskalis' hopper fleet active in West Africa alongside its Smit Lamnalco terminal towage in the region.

title: Boskalis converts Windpiper into world's largest (45,500 t) subsea rock installation vessel; in service 2026
summary: Boskalis announced the conversion of a newbuild hull into the 227 m, 45,500 t DP2 subsea rock installation vessel Windpiper with inclined fall pipe, delivered Q1 2026 after an 18-month conversion and deployed first to Baltic Power (Poland) in July 2026. Part of EUR 564m 2025 fleet capex that also includes the Seaway hopper and a 24,000 t cable-lay vessel ordered May 2026 for 2029.

title: Boskalis completes buy-out of Rezayat's 50% in Smit Lamnalco, taking full ownership
summary: After the Boluda sale stalled over Russia-seized vessels and sanctions, Boskalis agreed on 8 July 2024 and completed on 21 October 2024 the purchase of Saudi Rezayat Group's 50% of Smit Lamnalco (2023 revenue ~USD 275m, EBITDA ~USD 100m; ~160 vessels across four continents). Full consolidation from 1 November 2024 added just over EUR 1bn to the order book; the Australian/PNG harbour towage was then carved out and sold to Boluda in 2025.

title: Boskalis 2024: record EUR 4.36bn revenue, EUR 781m net profit, order book EUR 7.0bn
summary: Boskalis posted record 2024 results (revenue EUR 4,362m, EBITDA EUR 1,303m, net profit EUR 781m, solvency 56.3%) with EUR 5.3bn of new orders including just over EUR 1bn from consolidating Smit Lamnalco. Active dredging projects spanned Saudi Arabia, Singapore (Tuas Terminal 2, Pulau Tekong), Philippines (New Manila airport), Taiwan, Australia, Fehmarnbelt and Dutch/Belgian infrastructure; no African dredging projects were highlighted.

title: Damen wins EUR 49.5m Lithuanian Navy OPV 6711 pollution-response and SAR vessel
summary: Damen Workboats signed in Vilnius a EUR 49.5m contract (EUR 40m ERDF-funded) for a 67 m OPV 6711-based pollution-response and search-and-rescue vessel for the Lithuanian Navy, replacing the 1987-built Sakiai, with delivery by summer 2029. Illustrates Damen's continued strength in government/naval workboats in Europe.

title: Bankrupt Damen Shipyards Mangalia offered at fifth auction with 25% price cut to EUR 138m
summary: Damen Shipyards Mangalia (49% Damen, 51% Romanian state's SN 2 Mai), with three dry docks, 1,590 m of quay and 181,500 m2 of land on the Black Sea, is in bankruptcy; four auctions at the EUR 184m assessed value failed and a fifth on 9 October 2026 opened at EUR 138m, with a EUR 84m liquidation floor. Damen Holding appealed the sale mechanism. Rheinmetall and MSC reportedly won a EUR 138m auction in October 2026. Marks Damen's exit from its largest Black Sea repair/newbuild yard.

title: Damen signs long-term engine framework with Everllence for methanol-ready fuel-flexible tug range
summary: Damen and Everllence (ex-MAN Energy Solutions) agreed a long-term framework making the 175D high-speed engine (1,440-4,400 kW, methanol-ready) the series engine for Damen's new fuel-flexible ASD Tug 2512 FF, 2713 FF and 3313 FF, designed for later dual-fuel methanol or hybrid conversion. Standardises Damen's next-generation harbour tug offering to towage operators worldwide.

title: Damen unveils methanol-ready CFe 1100 hybrid container feeder design at SMM 2026
summary: Damen launched the 150 m CFe 1100 container feeder (1,100+ TEU, 174 reefer plugs, Ice Class 1A, two-stroke hybrid with 1,250 kW PTI, shore power, methanol-ready engine room and tank space, optional battery room) for regional and international feeder trades. Positions Damen as a supplier to feeder operators renewing fleets under FuelEU/ETS pressure, relevant to Unifeeder's newbuild choices.

title: Albwardy Damen lays keel in Sharjah for first-in-series MPV 4916 'Smokey' for Herman Senior
summary: Albwardy Damen's Sharjah yard laid the keel of Multi-Purpose Vessel 4916 Smokey, first of a new series for Herman Senior, continuing the UAE yard's shift from repair toward newbuilding (also building Multi Cats and Shoalbusters for stock, SAR vessels for Iraq's Jawar Al Khaleej and converting the heavy-lift Jawar 31). Albwardy Damen is Damen's main Gulf production and repair base.

title: Damen to build second RSD-E 2513 fully electric tug for AD Ports' Noatum Maritime at Khalifa Port
summary: Damen and Noatum Maritime (AD Ports Group) agreed a second compact fully electric RSD-E Tug 2513 for berthing at Khalifa Port, following Bu Tinah, the Middle East's first all-electric tug delivered in July 2024 (Damen Financial Services lease) which set a Guinness record of 78.2 t electric bollard pull in November 2024. Cements Damen as AD Ports' electric-tug supplier, a direct benchmark for DP World's P&O Maritime fleet decarbonisation.
capacity: 1 x electric RSD tug (~70 t BP)

title: Damen Technical Cooperation signs MoU with India's Square Port Shipyard, its third Indian-subcontinent partnership
summary: Square Port Shipyard (c.250 km south of Mumbai) and Damen Technical Cooperation signed an MoU to upgrade the yard to build Damen-design vessels for the regional market, including naval/defence vessels under Make in India. Damen's licensed-build model expands its Indian footprint as Cochin Shipyard and Swan Defence win Svitzer tug orders.

title: Al Seer Marine-Damen JV wins AED 1.3bn Tawazun contract for UAE Navy offshore patrol vessels
summary: The Al Seer Marine (IHC)-Damen International joint venture secured an AED 1.3bn (~USD 354m), four-year Tawazun Council contract to build advanced OPVs in the UAE for naval, coast guard, SAR and disaster-relief roles, with an integrated logistics support package. Builds on the Dune JV (2022), expanded in Nov 2024 into commercial shipbuilding with 26+ vessels planned for 2025.

title: Al Seer Marine and Damen expand Dune JV from naval into commercial shipbuilding and vessel management
summary: Al Seer Marine and Damen International announced the expansion of their 2022 Dune joint venture beyond naval shipbuilding into commercial newbuilds, technical/commercial vessel management, project management and vessel sale-and-purchase from UAE facilities, targeting 26+ vessels built in the UAE in 2025 for domestic and international clients.

title: Albwardy Damen to build Multi Cats and Shoalbuster for stock in UAE; delivers SAR vessels for Iraqi Ports Authority contract
summary: Albwardy Damen announced speculative construction of a Multi Cat 2712 (Nov 2025), Multi Cat 3313 SD (Dec 2025) and Shoalbuster 2711 (Feb 2026) for Gulf dredging and offshore demand, after handing over three Damen SAR vessels to Jawar Al Khaleej for a 20-year Iraqi Ports Authority contract and converting the 122 m Jawar 31 into a heavy-lift vessel. Signals Damen's bet on Gulf port/offshore construction growth.

title: Damen wins six-tug order from Zamil Offshore's Western Coast Port Services for Jeddah
summary: Albwardy Damen signed a contract with Western Coast Port Services (WCPS), a 2024-established subsidiary of Zamil Offshore, for six newbuild ASD tugs (five ASD 2813, one ASD 3212) to be built at Damen Song Cam, Vietnam, for harbour towage at Jeddah Islamic Port. One of Damen's largest recent Saudi tug orders and the fleet basis for Zamil's entry into Red Sea port services alongside DP World's Jeddah terminal.

title: Damen Song Cam delivers five harbour tugs to Boluda for Europe and West Africa
summary: Damen's Vietnamese yard delivered three RSD 2513 (80 t BP) and two ASD 2312 tugs to Boluda Towage in Q1 2026 for Rotterdam, Tilbury and Abidjan, following a Damen ASD 2813 (VB Marte) delivered to Boluda Italy in Dec 2025 and an ASD 2811 (VB Audace) for La Reunion in 2026. Confirms Damen as the principal newbuild supplier to the world's largest towage group.

title: ASRY completes SPS and upgrade of ADES jack-up Admarine 339, largest rig ever docked; becomes NOV-approved repair facility
summary: ASRY delivered the special periodic survey, drydocking and upgrade of ADES's JU-2000E jack-up Admarine 339, the largest drilling rig ever docked at the Bahrain yard, on time and on budget, and announced NOV approval allowing OEM-standard repair of drilling equipment in-house rather than shipping it abroad. Strengthens ASRY's rig-repair lead in the Gulf versus Drydocks World and IMI.

title: ASRY marks 200th offshore rig project with Valaris 250 'Bob Palmer' repair; targets MOPU conversion market
summary: ASRY's Offshore Division completed its 200th rig project, the repair and upgrade of Valaris' Gorilla-class jack-up Bob Palmer, with 700,000+ LTI-free man-hours. In January 2026 the yard reported concurrent work for Valaris, ADES, Saipem, EDC and GDI (ADES rigs prepared for Nigeria, Thailand and Brazil campaigns) and announced plans to enter the Mobile Offshore Production Unit conversion market in 2026.

title: ASRY and Priya Blue launch green ship recycling JV in Bahrain after first vessel arrives
summary: ASRY and India's Priya Blue Group formally launched a ship-recycling joint venture at the Hidd yard, with Best Oasis sourcing tonnage and ASRY providing dry docks, slipways and berths able to take vessels up to ULCC size and offshore assets (FPSOs, FSOs, rigs) directly onto berth, aligned with the Hong Kong Convention and EU SRR. First HKC/EU-grade recycling capacity in the Gulf, complementing ASRY's July 2025 recycling heads of terms with AD Ports and JM Baxi.

title: ASRY and Fincantieri sign MoU to explore naval and offshore shipbuilding up to 80 m in Bahrain
summary: ASRY and Italy's Fincantieri signed an MoU to assess design and construction of surface military vessels up to 80 m for the Bahrain Navy and Coast Guard, similar-sized offshore vessels, Gulf export opportunities and MRO for military, commercial and offshore vessels. Follows ASRY's Feb 2025 agreements with Leonardo and DE Wave and a Roboze additive-manufacturing facility, part of its diversification from repair into newbuilding.

title: ASRY completes fast-track repair of Torm product tanker Torm Venture in 14 days vs 18 planned
summary: ASRY completed an extensive repair and renewal docking of Torm's 18-year-old product tanker Torm Venture in 14 days against an 18-day estimate, a reference project for its core Gulf tanker-repair franchise (also covered by the January 2025 AMPTC fleet maintenance agreement and a May 2024 KOTC contract).

title: ASRY unveils 44.5 MW two-phase solar project with Kanoo CleanMax, billed as largest at any drydock
summary: ASRY and Kanoo CleanMax Renewables launched a solar power project of 22.5 MW in phase one (36m kWh/yr) and 22 MW in phase two (71m kWh/yr total), expected to save over USD 2m a year and described as the world's largest solar installation at a drydock. Supports ASRY's green-yard positioning for owners under IMO/EU decarbonisation pressure.

title: ASRY launches two self-propelled bunker vessels built for Bapco Refining
summary: ASRY launched two self-propelled fuel-oil bunker barges for Bapco Refining at Hidd after a keel laying in September 2024, in what ASRY called one of the largest projects it has secured and part of a strategic alliance with Bapco to position Bahrain as a maritime hub. Commissioning and sea trials follow. Demonstrates ASRY's return to newbuilding for the regional energy sector.

title: AD Ports Group and ASRY sign three heads of terms: GCC shipyard/drydock JV, ship recycling with JM Baxi, port infrastructure
summary: AD Ports Group and ASRY signed heads of terms to (1) form a joint venture to manage drydocks and shipyards across the GCC with possible expansion beyond, (2) develop environmentally responsible ship-recycling facilities with India's JM Baxi, and (3) explore joint port and terminal infrastructure investments via a working group. Extends the Noatum-ASRY marine services JV into a strategic AD Ports-ASRY alliance that could create a regional drydocking rival to Drydocks World.

title: ASRY Marine, the Noatum Maritime-ASRY towage JV, starts operations with four ASD tugs at Hidd
summary: ASRY and AD Ports' Noatum Maritime formed ASRY Marine (announced Feb/Mar 2025) to provide towage, mooring and integrated marine services in Bahrain and the region; four Noatum ASD tugs and a mooring boat arrived at Hidd in May 2025, replacing ASRY's old fleet. ASRY also signed an AtkinsRealis MoU on offshore wind work. Brings AD Ports' marine services arm into Bahrain in competition with Svitzer Bahrain.

title: ASRY signs MoU with Abu Dhabi Ship Building to co-build naval auxiliary vessels and port craft
summary: Alongside the Noatum marine-services JV, ASRY signed an MoU with EDGE Group's Abu Dhabi Ship Building (ADSB) to jointly build naval auxiliary vessels and port craft, pairing ASRY's facilities with ADSB's naval design and build expertise. Part of a string of 2025 shipbuilding partnerships (Leonardo, DE Wave, Fincantieri) aimed at diversifying ASRY into newbuild.

title: ASRY signs agreements with Leonardo (naval repair/conversion) and DE Wave (cruise ship repair) during Italian PM visit
summary: During Italian Prime Minister Meloni's visit to Bahrain, ASRY signed partnerships with Leonardo to pursue naval repair and conversion work and with DE Wave to attract cruise ship repairs and conversions to Bahrain. Targets two higher-value segments beyond ASRY's traditional tanker and rig repair base.

title: ASRY signs docking and maintenance agreement for AMPTC's tanker and gas carrier fleet
summary: ASRY signed a fleet docking and maintenance agreement with the Arab Maritime Petroleum Transport Company (AMPTC), which operates 12 product tankers and two LPG carriers with four gas carrier newbuilds due 2026-27. Secures recurring Gulf tanker repair volume following a 2024 Kuwait Oil Tanker Company tender win.

title: Kuwait Oil Tanker Company awards ASRY tanker repair contract after regional tender
summary: ASRY won a regional tender from Kuwait Oil Tanker Company (KOTC) for tanker docking/repair work, reinforcing its position as the Gulf's main independent tanker repair yard ahead of the 2025 AMPTC and Torm jobs. Details of scope and duration were not available (article paywalled).

title: Qatar Shipyard Technology Solutions (ex-N-KOM) signs Wartsila MoU for engine, retrofit and decarbonisation services at Ras Laffan
summary: QSTS, the Nakilat-Keppel JV rebranded from N-KOM in December 2023 and operating the Erhama Bin Jaber Al Jalahma Shipyard at Ras Laffan, signed an MoU with Wartsila to offer 2- and 4-stroke engine and propulsion maintenance, de-rating, dual-fuel conversions and decarbonisation advisory to vessels (notably modern LNG carriers) calling for repair. New CEO Jos Goris frames it as broadening the yard's specialist offering to international owners.

title: Qatar Shipyard Technology Solutions signs MoU with Armada Technologies for hull air-lubrication retrofits
summary: QSTS (formerly N-KOM) and UK-based Armada Technologies agreed to assess a commercial tie-up to install Passive Air Lubrication Systems on customers' vessels during docking at Ras Laffan, with Armada providing fuel-saving estimates and design support. Part of the yard's post-rebrand push into energy-efficiency retrofits, following earlier MoUs with Cryo Pump Repair and MAN for LNG carrier equipment.

title: Nakilat H1 2026: ship repair, towage and agency segment declines on regional disruption while group profit holds at QAR 857m
summary: Nakilat reported H1 2026 net profit of QAR 857m (QAR 860m in H1 2025) and said its Marine Services segment, which includes the QSTS/N-KOM ship repair JV at Ras Laffan plus towage and shipping agency, declined because of the regional security situation and Gulf shipping disruption, prompting cost-control measures. Indicates reduced third-party docking activity at the Qatari yard during 2026.

title: Cochin Shipyard and Drydocks World (DP World) form 50:50 JV to operate and expand Cochin International Ship Repair Facility
summary: At the BRICS Summit in New Delhi, Cochin Shipyard and DP World's Drydocks World signed a 50:50 joint venture agreement to operate and expand the International Ship Repair Facility (ISRF) in Cochin, formalising their April 2025 MoU on repair clusters at Kochi and Vadinar and offshore fabrication. The partners commit to add capacity for Indian, regional and international vessels; Drydocks World sees further Indian repair/fabrication expansion. Note: this records Cochin Shipyard's activity; the partner is DP World's own Drydocks World.

title: Cochin Shipyard delivers MS Maria, second of eight 7,000 dwt HS EcoFreighter MPVs for Germany's HS Schiffahrts
summary: Cochin Shipyard delivered MS Maria, the second of eight 7,000 dwt HS EcoFreighter multipurpose vessels ordered by German owner HS Schiffahrts, confirming its growing export order book in European short-sea tonnage alongside tugs, SOVs and dredgers.

title: ABB to supply power and propulsion for two Cochin Shipyard electric tugs under India's Green Tug Transition Programme
summary: Cochin Shipyard awarded ABB the electrical, propulsion, automation and digital systems (Onboard DC Grid, PEMS, remote diagnostics) for two battery-electric tugs being built for Polestar Maritime to operate at Jawaharlal Nehru Port under Phase 1 of the Green Tug Transition Programme, with delivery in 2027. Positions CSL as India's lead builder of green tugs for major ports.

title: Cochin Shipyard and HBL Engineering form JV for maritime battery and energy-storage systems
summary: Cochin Shipyard signed a joint venture agreement with HBL Engineering to develop and commercialise marine batteries, battery management systems, electric motors, power electronics and charging infrastructure for domestic and export markets, supporting the electric tug and hybrid SOV programmes it is building for Svitzer, Polestar and North Star.

title: Cochin Shipyard cuts steel on two 70 t ASTDS tugs for Polestar; order book holds 17 ASTDS tugs plus six green-design tugs
summary: Cochin Shipyard held a steel-cutting ceremony for two Robert Allan-designed 33 m, 70 t BP harbour tugs for Polestar Maritime (IRS class, Niigata engines), disclosing an order book of 17 Approved Standard Tug Design tugs plus six environmentally friendly tugs. With Adani's 13 tugs and Svitzer's electric series, CSL has become India's dominant tug builder.

title: Cochin Shipyard wins Svitzer contract for four (+4) battery-electric TRAnsverse 2600e tugs, first for export to a global towage major
summary: Following a November 2025 letter of intent at India Maritime Week, Cochin Shipyard signed a shipbuilding contract with Svitzer for at least four 26 m fully electric TRAnsverse 2600e tugs (70 t BP, Robert Allan design) with options for four more; construction began in September 2026 with first delivery in late 2027. CSL's first series order from a global towage operator, validating its ambition to become an export hub for green harbour craft.

title: Cochin Shipyard lays keel of second hybrid-electric SOV for UK's North Star
summary: Cochin Shipyard laid the keel of the second of two DNV-classed hybrid electric Service Operation Vessels for Aberdeen-based North Star (lithium-ion DC power, electric azimuth propulsion, DP2, walk-to-work gangway, 80 berths), serving European offshore wind. Demonstrates CSL's reach into complex European offshore-renewables tonnage.

title: Cochin Shipyard and Seatrium Offshore Technology sign MoU for offshore MRO and fabrication across India and Asia
summary: CSL and Singapore's Seatrium Offshore Technology agreed to cooperate on offshore maintenance, repair and overhaul and fabrication for Asian clients, combining Seatrium's engineering and equipment with CSL's infrastructure and repair experience, with potential expansion to other regional offshore markets. Seatrium called India a key long-term growth market.

title: Cochin Shipyard signs HD KSOE large-vessel partnership and plans INR 3,700 cr Kochi block facility and INR 15,000 cr Tamil Nadu greenfield yard
summary: At the Samudra se Samriddhi summit in Gujarat, CSL signed MoUs with HD Korea Shipbuilding & Offshore Engineering to jointly build large commercial vessels using its new 310 m dry dock, and with Guidance Tamil Nadu for a ~INR 15,000 crore (~USD 1.8bn) greenfield shipyard with repair facility (10,000 jobs phase 1). It also announced a INR 3,700 crore Kochi Block Fabrication Facility (80 acres, 120,000 t/yr, 2,000 jobs). India's largest shipbuilding capacity push, backed by Korean technology.
capacity: 120,000 t/yr block facility; 310 m dry dock

title: Cochin Shipyard and HD KSOE sign long-term shipbuilding cooperation MoU; CSL wins two more Polestar tugs
summary: CSL and HD Korea Shipbuilding & Offshore Engineering (parent of Hyundai Heavy, Mipo and Samho) signed a long-term MoU to jointly pursue newbuild projects in India and abroad, share know-how, raise productivity and upskill workers. CSL simultaneously booked two 70 t Robert Allan tugs from Polestar Maritime, to be built with subsidiary Udupi-CSL, following three similar units.

title: Cochin Shipyard signs MoU with A.P. Moller-Maersk on ship repair, dry docking, shipbuilding and seafarer training in India
summary: CSL and Maersk agreed to explore cooperation on ship repair and dry docking of Maersk vessels in India, new shipbuilding projects, technical standards sharing and joint training, leveraging CSL's large dry dock and upcoming International Ship Repair Facility. Analysts expected margin upside; CSL's Q3 FY25 revenue rose 8.6% to INR 1,148 crore. Links a top container line's repair demand to the yard DP World's Drydocks World later joined as JV partner.

title: Adani Ports orders eight harbour tugs from Cochin Shipyard, lifting CSL's Adani order book to 13
summary: APSEZ placed an order for eight harbour tugs with Cochin Shipyard for delivery between December 2026 and May 2028, adding to three ASD tugs already under construction (two earlier units went to Paradeep and New Mangalore). Reinforces CSL as the captive tug supplier to India's largest private port group, a DP World competitor.

title: Cochin Shipyard lays keel of DCI Dredge Godavari, India's largest (12,000 m3) hopper dredger, with Royal IHC design
summary: CSL laid the keel of the 127 m, 12,000 m3 trailing suction hopper dredger DCI Dredge Godavari for Dredging Corporation of India, designed with Royal IHC, the largest dredger built in India. Adds capital dredging tonnage to CSL's diversified portfolio and supports Indian port deepening programmes.

title: Zamil Offshore launches Western Coast Port Services at Jeddah and orders six Damen ASD tugs
summary: Zamil Offshore established Western Coast Port Services (WCPS) in 2024 as a Red Sea port services subsidiary and signed with Albwardy Damen for six newbuild ASD tugs (five ASD 2813, one ASD 3212), to be built at Damen Song Cam in Vietnam, for harbour towage at Jeddah Islamic Port. Marks Zamil's expansion from Gulf offshore support and its Dammam shipyard into Red Sea harbour towage at the port where DP World operates the South Container Terminal.

title: Bahri orders three 320,000 dwt VLCCs from IMI for SAR 1.69bn, first Saudi-built VLCCs
summary: Bahri contracted International Maritime Industries to build three 320,000 dwt VLCCs at Ras Al-Khair for about SAR 1.692bn (~USD 451m), with phased delivery in 2029-2030, bringing Bahri's Saudi-built orders in 2025-26 to nine vessels (six Ultramaxes plus three VLCCs). The first VLCCs ever ordered from a Saudi yard, a milestone for IMI's Aramco/Bahri/HD Hyundai/Lamprell joint venture and for Saudi maritime localisation.

title: IMI and Lamprell sign agreement to build offshore production platforms and jackets at Ras Al-Khair
summary: IMI and founding shareholder Lamprell signed an agreement to manufacture a series of offshore structures including production platforms and jackets at the Ras Al-Khair yard, the first time such structures will be built there. CEO Abdullah Al-Ghamdi called it a defining step beyond rig and ship newbuild/repair, taking IMI into Aramco offshore fabrication work historically done in the UAE.

title: Bahri orders six geared Ultramax bulk carriers from IMI, Saudi Arabia's first large-scale commercial shipbuilding order
summary: Bahri ordered six geared Ultramax bulk carriers from IMI's Ras Al-Khair yard, described as the Kingdom's first large-scale shipbuilding project. Once fully operational the yard targets up to six rigs and 40+ vessels a year including VLCCs, plus repair of up to 250 vessels and 15 rigs annually, making IMI a potential Gulf repair competitor to Drydocks World and ASRY.

title: IMI signs ARO Drilling contract for Kingdom 3, first jack-up rig built entirely in Saudi Arabia
summary: IMI and Aramco Rowan Offshore Drilling (ARO) signed a contract and started construction of Kingdom 3, an S116E jack-up and the first drilling rig to be built completely in Saudi Arabia at Ras Al-Khair, after earlier ARO rigs were partly built at Lamprell's Hamriyah yard. IMI's full-capacity target is six jack-ups, 25 OSVs and 18 large commercial vessels a year.
